entries.question: How many times did Jesus appear after His resurrection?
alt_phrasings: how many times did jesus appear after his resurrection
how many times did jesus appear after he rose from the dead
post-resurrection appearances of jesus
how many post resurrection appearances of jesus are recorded
entries.answer: No single verse gives a total count. Harmonizing the four Gospels, Acts, and 1 Corinthians 15, roughly 10-11 distinct appearances before the ascension are traditionally recognized: to Mary Magdalene, to the other women, to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, to Peter alone, to ten disciples (Thomas absent) behind locked doors, to the Eleven eight days later (Thomas present), to seven disciples by the Sea of Galilee, to the Eleven on a mountain in Galilee, to more than 500 believers at once, to James, and to all the apostles at the ascension.
entries.note: 1 Corinthians 15:5-8 is the closest thing scripture has to a summary list, but even it doesn't total the earlier Gospel appearances against its own list -- the ~10-11 figure is a harmonization, not a stated number. John 21:14 explicitly calls the Galilee/Tiberias appearance the disciples' 'third' time seeing Him as a group, which is one data point this harmonization rests on.

By the crucifixion, Jesus entrusts Mary's care to the disciple John rather than to Joseph -- widely taken as evidence Joseph had already died by then -- but that is an inference from the text, not a stated fact, and no age is ever given.
entries.note: Any specific age or year of death you may see elsewhere (art, tradition, devotional writing) is extra-biblical -- it is not in the canonical text bundled with this app.

entries.question: What languages was the Bible originally written in?

what language was the new testament written in
original languages of scripture
entries.answer: The Old Testament was written mainly in Hebrew, with a few passages in Aramaic (parts of Daniel and Ezra). The New Testament was written in Koine Greek.
entries.note: This is the standard position of textual scholarship on the manuscripts, not something a single verse states about itself.

entries.question: Who wrote the most books in the New Testament?
alt_phrasings: which new testament author wrote the most books
who is the author of most of the new testament
entries.answer: Paul, traditionally credited as author of 13 New Testament letters -- more than any other named writer. A 14th, Hebrews, is anonymous in the text itself and has traditionally been attributed to Paul by some, though that authorship has long been disputed by scholars.
entries.note: Excluding the disputed Hebrews, Paul's 13 undisputed letters already outnumber any other single author's contribution to the New Testament.

entries.question: Who was the oldest person in the Bible?

who was the longest living person in scripture

what were the names of jesus's brothers

entries.question: Who were the kings of the united kingdom of Israel?
alt_phrasings: who were the three kings before the kingdom divided
kings of israel before the split

entries.question: How many miracles did Jesus perform?
alt_phrasings: how many miracles are recorded in the gospels
total number of jesus's miracles
entries.answer: No total is given. Scripture explicitly says not every miracle was recorded -- John's Gospel closes by saying Jesus did many other signs, and even more that if all were written down, the world itself could not contain the books. Popular lists commonly catalogue around 35 distinct miracles that are specifically narrated across the four Gospels, but that is a count of what's written down, not a claim about how many Jesus actually performed.

entries.question: How many times did the Israelites rebel against God?
alt_phrasings: how many times did the israelites rebel
how many times did israel rebel in the wilderness
entries.answer: Ten times, per God's own count in Numbers 14:22 -- after the report of the twelve spies, God says of that generation: "not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tested Me these ten times and have not obeyed My voice, will ever see the land." Scripture doesn't list all ten as one numbered set in a single place -- traditional Jewish and Christian reckonings compile them from incidents across Exodus and Numbers (e.g. the Red Sea, Marah, the wilderness of Sin, Rephidim/testing at Massah, the golden calf, Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah, the spies' report at Kadesh).
entries.note: The number ten is scripture's own; the specific list of which ten incidents is a traditional compilation, not itself one scriptural list.

entries.question: How many days was Jonah in the fish's belly?
alt_phrasings: how many days was jonah in the whale's stomach
how long was jonah inside the whale
how many days and nights was jonah in the fish
entries.answer: Three days and three nights. Jonah 1:17: "the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights." Jesus later points to this exact span as a sign of His own coming burial and resurrection.

citations.role: Jesus references the same three days and three nights

entries.note: Scripture calls it a "great fish," not a whale -- "whale" comes from popular retelling (and older English translations of the Greek word in Matthew 12:40), not the Hebrew text of Jonah itself.

entries.question: How many miracles happened in the Old Testament?
alt_phrasings: how many miracles are in the old testament
total number of old testament miracles
entries.answer: No total is given anywhere in scripture. The Old Testament records many miracles in clusters rather than as one running count -- among them the ten plagues on Egypt, the parting of the Red Sea, the pillar of cloud and fire, manna and water from the rock in the wilderness, the sun standing still for Joshua, and a dense concentration of miracles around the prophets Elijah and Elisha (fire from heaven, raising the dead, multiplying oil and flour, healing Naaman's leprosy, and more).
entries.note: As with Jesus's miracles, this app won't state a precise total that scripture itself never gives -- popular tallies exist but are counts of what's recorded, compiled after the fact, not a number scripture states.

entries.question: How many times does God speak audibly to His people in scripture?
alt_phrasings: how many time does god talk loudly to his people
how many times does god speak loudly
how often does god speak audibly in the bible
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't define "loudly" as its own category or give a total count of audible-voice events, so this app won't invent one. Notable instances include the audible voice and trumpet-like sound at Sinai when the Ten Commandments were given (Exodus 19:16-19; 20:1), the "still small voice" to Elijah (deliberately contrasted with a great wind, an earthquake, and fire -- not loud at all), and the voice from heaven at Jesus's baptism, at the Transfiguration, and shortly before His crucifixion. On the giving of the Ten Commandments specifically, Matthew Henry's commentary on Exodus 20:1 observes: "he never spoke, at any time, upon any occasion, as he spoke the ten commandments... They were not only spoken audibly... but with a great deal of dreadful pomp." That is Matthew Henry's own characterization of Sinai as uniquely dramatic among these events -- his interpretive judgment, not a scriptural head-count.

entries.question: How many prophets were there in the Old Testament?
alt_phrasings: how many old testament prophets are there
total number of prophets in the bible
entries.answer: Scripture gives no single total. A well-known Jewish tradition (the Talmud, Megillah 14a) counts 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses across the Hebrew Bible -- but that count is rabbinic tradition, not a Bible verse. Separately, and on firmer textual ground, the Old Testament contains 17 books traditionally classed as prophetic: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, and Daniel (the "major" prophets), plus the twelve "minor" prophets from Hosea through Malachi -- alongside many other named prophets, such as Elijah, Elisha, Nathan, and Gad, who have no book of their own.

citations.role: example: Elijah, a prophet with no book of his own
example: Nathan, a prophet with no book of his own

entries.note: The 48+7 figure is Jewish tradition (Talmud), included here clearly labeled as such -- not a number scripture itself states.

entries.question: Who was Moses?
alt_phrasings: tell me about moses
what did moses do
entries.answer: Moses was a Hebrew born in Egypt during Pharaoh's decree to kill Hebrew infant boys, hidden and then raised in Pharaoh's own household after being drawn from the Nile. After killing an Egyptian overseer, he fled to Midian, where God called him at the burning bush to lead Israel out of slavery. He confronted Pharaoh, led the Exodus and the crossing of the Red Sea, received the Law (including the Ten Commandments) from God at Mount Sinai, and led Israel through 40 years in the wilderness. He died on Mount Nebo, having seen the Promised Land but not entered it, and scripture calls him unique among Israel's prophets: "no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face."

entries.question: What is the purpose of being saved?
alt_phrasings: why does god save people
what is salvation for
what is the point of being saved
entries.answer: Scripture gives several purposes directly, rather than a single one: salvation is by grace, through faith, not by good works -- so that no one can boast -- and yet it is FOR good works, which God prepared in advance (Ephesians 2:8-10). Paul describes it as being conformed to the likeness of Christ (Romans 8:29). Peter describes believers as a people chosen and called "to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light" (1 Peter 2:9).
entries.note: These are direct scriptural statements, not this app's own theological summary. Different Christian traditions place different weight and additional detail on this question; consult the bundled commentaries (Commentaries tab) for denominationally varied fuller treatments.

entries.question: How do you become saved?
alt_phrasings: how do you get saved
how can i be saved
what must i do to be saved
how do you become born again
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus says, "unless someone is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God" -- born of water and of the Spirit (John 3:3-7) -- and preaches, "Repent and believe in the gospel!" (Mark 1:15). Peter says, "Repent and be baptized... and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:38); Paul and Silas tell the jailer, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved" (Acts 16:31); and Paul writes, "if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved... everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" (Romans 10:9-13). It is "by grace you have been saved through faith... not by works, so that no one can boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9), and the price was the blood of Christ: we were redeemed "with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot" (1 Peter 1:18-19; Ephesians 1:7).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: a person is saved by turning from sin in repentance and trusting in the shed blood of Jesus Christ -- His death and resurrection -- and is then born again by the Holy Spirit, becoming a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17). The new birth is followed by water baptism and by the promise of the baptism in the Holy Spirit for a Spirit-filled life (Acts 2:38-39).

Other views: Christian traditions differ on the role of baptism, the sacraments and works, and on whether salvation can be lost; see those questions for the range.

citations.role: stated: redeemed by the precious blood of Christ

entries.question: What is eternal life?
alt_phrasings: define eternal life
meaning of eternal life
entries.answer: Scripture defines it directly, in Jesus's own words: "Now this is eternal life: that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent" (John 17:3). It is described not merely as unending existence but as a relationship of knowing God through Christ.

entries.question: How do you get eternal life?

entries.answer: "For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life" (John 3:16). Paul states it as a gift rather than a wage: "the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23).

entries.answer: 1. No other gods before Me. 2. No idols/carved images. 3. Do not take the LORD's name in vain. 4. Keep the Sabbath holy. 5. Honor your father and mother. 6. Do not murder. 7. Do not commit adultery. 8. Do not steal. 9. Do not bear false witness. 10. Do not covet. Given by God to Moses at Mount Sinai; scripture records the full text twice.

entries.question: What is the new covenant?
alt_phrasings: what does the new covenant mean
explain the new covenant
entries.answer: A covenant God promised through the prophet Jeremiah, distinct from the old covenant made at Sinai: "I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts... No longer will each man teach his neighbor... because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest... For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more" (Jeremiah 31:31-34). Hebrews 8 quotes this prophecy directly and identifies it as fulfilled in Christ, whose ministry as mediator Hebrews calls superior to the old covenant. At the Last Supper, Jesus Himself ties it to His own blood: "This cup is the new covenant in My blood."

entries.question: What is the old covenant?
alt_phrasings: what does the old covenant mean
explain the old covenant
what was the covenant at sinai
entries.answer: The covenant God made with Israel through Moses at Mount Sinai, with the Ten Commandments and the Law as its terms: obedience brings blessing, disobedience brings curses. Hebrews 8 contrasts it directly with the new covenant, quoting Jeremiah's prophecy and concluding: "By calling this covenant 'new,' He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear." This is a distinct question from "What is the new covenant?" -- old and new are contrasted with each other throughout Hebrews 8, not the same covenant.

entries.question: Is Jesus God?
alt_phrasings: is jesus divine
was jesus fully god
entries.answer: Yes. Scripture directly calls Him God, attributes divine characteristics to Him, and shows Him receiving worship -- "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (John 1:1); Thomas addresses the risen Jesus as "My Lord and my God!" (John 20:28).

entries.question: How can there be one God, yet three Persons (the Trinity)?
alt_phrasings: what is the trinity
explain the trinity
is god one or three
how can god be three and one
can the trinity be understood
entries.answer:
Scripture: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4), and "there is no God but Me" (Isaiah 45:5). Yet the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are each called God and are shown together: Jesus commands baptism "in the name" -- singular -- "of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19); at Jesus's baptism the Son is in the water, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father speaks from heaven (Matthew 3:16-17); Jesus says, "I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate... the Spirit of truth" (John 14:16-17); "the Word was God" (John 1:1); and lying to the Holy Spirit is lying to God (Acts 5:3-4). Paul closes with a blessing from all three (2 Corinthians 13:14). The three share one mind: Jesus says, "I and the Father are one," and that whoever has seen Him has seen the Father (John 10:30; 14:9-11); the Spirit "searches all things, even the depths of God," and knows the thoughts of God (1 Corinthians 2:10-11); and the Spirit speaks what He hears and takes from what is Christ's (John 16:13-15). And scripture is plain that God is beyond our full understanding: "as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts" (Isaiah 55:8-9); "O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!" (Romans 11:33-34).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the Trinity is a mystery that our minds cannot fully grasp -- the three is one and the one is three. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one and the same being, so they know each other's mind perfectly and are never at odds; yet that one God takes up three different roles in three different persons -- God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit. The Father plans and sends, the Son redeems by His blood, and the Spirit indwells and empowers, all working together as one God. A familiar picture is the gears of a clock: separate parts with different jobs that together make one working clock, none of them apart from the others. Like every illustration it falls short in one respect: scripture does not present the Father, Son and Spirit as parts of God but as each fully God (Colossians 2:9; Acts 5:3-4), and it shows all three at once and distinct -- as at Jesus's baptism -- so they are three persons in one God rather than one person known by three roles. Where the Son says He does not know the day or hour of His return (Mark 13:32), this is understood as knowledge withheld from us, not knowledge lacking in God: the Father set the times by His own authority and it was not meant for us to know (Acts 1:7), just as Jesus often spoke in parables that kept some things undisclosed (Matthew 13:10-17, 34-35). The Son knows; it was simply not to be revealed to us.

Other views: Oneness Pentecostals teach that God is a single person who shows Himself in three modes (Father, Son and Spirit) rather than as three distinct persons; Jehovah's Witnesses and others reject the Trinity altogether. Some read Mark 13:32 differently, as the Son in His human life on earth having "emptied Himself" (Philippians 2:7) of the exercise of some knowledge.

entries.question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
alt_phrasings: what is the holy spirit
is the holy spirit a person or a force
entries.answer: The Holy Spirit is presented as a personal being, not merely a force -- one who can be lied to (Acts 5:3-4), who intercedes (Romans 8:26), and whom Jesus calls a Helper who will guide believers into truth (John 14:16-17).

entries.question: If God is good, why does He allow suffering and evil?
alt_phrasings: why does god allow suffering
why is there evil in the world
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't give one single-verse answer; several strands run through it: sin's entry into a good creation brought brokenness (Genesis 3:17-19), God can work even harmful acts toward good ends (Genesis 50:20, of Joseph's brothers selling him into slavery), present suffering works toward a larger purpose for those who love God (Romans 8:28), and suffering is not the final word -- it will one day be ended entirely (Revelation 21:4). This remains one of theology's most discussed questions (the "problem of evil"), and different Christian traditions emphasize different parts of this answer.

entries.question: Did God create Satan, and how did Satan fall?
alt_phrasings: how did satan become evil
who is lucifer
entries.answer:
Scripture: Satan is a created being -- all thrones, powers, rulers and authorities were created through and for Christ (Colossians 1:16). Jesus said, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (Luke 10:18); Revelation 12:7-9 describes war in heaven in which the dragon, "that ancient serpent, called the devil and Satan," and his angels are thrown down; Jude 6 and 2 Peter 2:4 speak of angels who did not keep their positions; and 1 Timothy 3:6 warns against conceit that brings "the same judgment as the devil," pointing to pride.

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: God created Satan as a glorious angel -- the "anointed guardian cherub" who was "in Eden, the garden of God" -- who fell through pride and rebelled, drawing a third of the angels with him (Revelation 12:4). Many read Isaiah 14:12-15 ("How you have fallen from heaven, O morning star, son of the dawn!") and Ezekiel 28:12-17 as describing his fall behind the words spoken to the kings of Babylon and Tyre, because the language reaches beyond anything true of a mere man.

Other views: in their immediate context those two passages are addressed to human kings, so the name "Lucifer" (Latin for "morning star" in Isaiah 14:12) and the identification with Satan is an interpretive tradition rather than a direct scriptural statement; the fall itself is directly stated in Luke 10:18 and Revelation 12.
