entries.question: What is church discipline?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about church discipline
how should a church handle unrepentant sin
entries.answer: A formal process Jesus outlines for confronting an unrepentant believer: go to them privately first, then with one or two witnesses, then before the church, with removal from fellowship as a last resort if they still refuse to repent (Matthew 18:15-17). Paul instructs the Corinthian church to remove an unrepentant member from fellowship for the purpose of ultimately restoring him (1 Corinthians 5:1-5), and Galatians instructs restoring a fallen believer "gently," watching one's own heart in the process (Galatians 6:1).

entries.question: What is the biblical definition of the church?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible mean by the church
is the church a building
entries.answer: Not a building, but people: "the church, which is His body" (Colossians 1:18; Ephesians 1:22-23) -- the global body of all true believers in Jesus Christ, described as "in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body" (1 Corinthians 12:13), manifesting locally in specific congregations that gather.

entries.question: What are the biblical ordinances for the local church?
alt_phrasings: what are the sacraments of the church
what did jesus command the church to practice
entries.answer:
Scripture: Jesus commands His disciples to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19), and gave the Lord's Supper with the command to keep doing it in remembrance of Him (Luke 22:19; 1 Corinthians 11:23-26). He also washed His disciples' feet and told them to do as He had done (John 13:14-15).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: two ordinances instituted by Christ -- water baptism by immersion, and the Lord's Supper -- observed as acts of obedience and testimony rather than as channels of saving grace. Some Pentecostal and holiness churches also observe foot washing as an ordinance (John 13:14-15).

Other views: the Catholic and Orthodox churches teach seven sacraments (baptism, confirmation, the Eucharist, penance, anointing of the sick, holy orders and matrimony) as means of grace.

entries.question: What is the role of a church deacon?
alt_phrasings: what does a deacon do
what are the qualifications for a deacon
entries.answer: The role originates with seven men chosen to manage the daily distribution of food to widows, freeing the apostles to focus on prayer and preaching (Acts 6:1-6) -- deacons are described as qualified servants who manage practical, administrative, and charitable needs within the church, with specific character qualifications listed in 1 Timothy 3:8-13.

entries.question: Can a Christian see a secular therapist or psychiatrist?
alt_phrasings: is it okay for christians to go to therapy
can christians take medication for mental health
entries.answer: Scripture doesn't address modern psychiatry or therapy directly, so this is an application of broader principles rather than a direct command: seeking wise counsel is commended generally ("plans succeed with many advisers," Proverbs 11:14), while believers are cautioned to "test all things. Hold fast to what is good" (1 Thessalonians 5:21) and not to be taken captive by thinking that contradicts Christ (Colossians 2:8). Most Christian traditions today affirm that medical/psychological treatment can address real biological and psychological factors alongside -- not instead of -- spiritual care, with all advice filtered through scripture.
entries.note: The source document cited a nonexistent reference ("Protestants 11:14") here -- corrected to Proverbs 11:14, the most plausible intended verse, when this entry was checked against scripture.

entries.question: How should a Christian handle anxiety and depression?
alt_phrasings: what does the bible say about anxiety
how do christians deal with depression
entries.answer: "Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God" (Philippians 4:6-7); "Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you" (1 Peter 5:7); the psalmist models honest lament in the midst of depression: "Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me?" (Psalm 42:11). Most Christian traditions today also affirm pursuing medical treatment for depression/anxiety with a biological component, alongside prayer and Christian community, rather than treating these practices as opposed to each other.

entries.question: How can I discover my spiritual gifts?
alt_phrasings: how do i find my spiritual gift
what are the spiritual gifts
entries.answer: Scripture names various specific gifts (Romans 12:6-8; 1 Corinthians 12:4-7) given "to each one... for the common good," but doesn't prescribe a step-by-step discovery process. The commonly taught practical approach is active service in a local church, noticing where that service bears fruit, and receiving confirmation from church leadership and community (1 Peter 4:10, "use whatever gift you have received to serve others").

entries.question: What does it mean to take care of your body as a temple?
alt_phrasings: what does body as a temple mean
why does the bible say the body is a temple
entries.answer: "Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you... You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20) -- treating one's physical body, which belongs to God and houses His Spirit, with respect, avoiding what scripture elsewhere names as harmful (sexual immorality, substance abuse) and doing all things, including eating and drinking, for God's glory (1 Corinthians 10:31; Romans 12:1).

entries.question: How do I balance supporting family with helping the poor?
alt_phrasings: does the bible say to help family first or the poor
who comes first family or charity
entries.answer: Scripture places providing for one's own family as a serious, primary obligation -- "If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever" (1 Timothy 5:8) -- while also commanding generosity toward the vulnerable: "Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress" (James 1:27); "Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD" (Proverbs 19:17); giving is to flow "out of... abundance," for a fair balance, not at the expense of one's own basic needs (2 Corinthians 8:13-14).

entries.question: What does the blood of Jesus do?
alt_phrasings: is the blood of jesus enough to save me
what does it mean to be washed in the blood
what does it mean that jesus's blood bought us
why is the blood of jesus important
what does the bible say about the blood of jesus
what does blood bought mean
entries.answer:
Scripture: the blood of Jesus bought us. The church of God was "purchased with His own blood" (Acts 20:28); "you were bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:20); we were redeemed "not with perishable things such as silver or gold... but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot" (1 Peter 1:18-19); and the redeemed sing to the Lamb, "by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation" (Revelation 5:9). It washes away our sin: "the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7); in Him "we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses" (Ephesians 1:7); and those before the throne "have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb" (Revelation 7:14). It is God's appointed payment for sin: "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness" (Hebrews 9:22; Leviticus 17:11), foreshadowed when the blood on the doorposts made the LORD pass over Israel's houses (Exodus 12:13). Through it we are justified and saved from wrath (Romans 5:9), have peace with God through "the blood of His cross" (Colossians 1:20), and have "confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus" (Hebrews 10:19). Believers overcome the accuser "by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony" (Revelation 12:11).

Pentecostal / evangelical understanding: the blood-bought life. The death and shed blood of Jesus are the once-for-all price that redeems the sinner from sin, death and the power of the enemy. Yes, the blood is enough to save -- there is nothing to add to it, and the gift is received freely by repentance and faith (Romans 3:25). Because we were bought with a price, we belong to Him (1 Corinthians 6:19-20) and are called to live as His purified people, "zealous for good deeds" (Titus 2:14). The blood is never a license to keep on sinning: to go on deliberately sinning is to trample the Son of God underfoot and treat "the blood of the covenant" as unclean (Hebrews 10:26-29). Believers plead the blood in prayer for cleansing, protection and victory over the enemy (Revelation 12:11).

Other views: Christian traditions explain the atonement in different ways (as substitution, as ransom, as victory over evil), and Catholic and Orthodox teaching links the blood of Christ closely with the Eucharist; all affirm that the cross is the basis of forgiveness.
